section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the redemption was an open miracle above nature, yet clothed in nature, because the revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof, which transcends both Sovev and Memaleh, united miracle and nature.
section.t: And it can be said,
that this is that the redemption
(of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud-Beis Tammuz)
was an open miracle above nature,
and nevertheless, the miracle was clothed in nature,
and although the miracle was clothed in nature, this was in a manner that nature did not conceal or hide the miracle,
to the extent that all the ends of the earth saw that this was an open miracle,
for the root of nature is from the Name Elokim,
Memaleh,
and the root of miracles is from the Name Havayah,
Sovev,
and since in the redemption there was the revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above Sovev and Memaleh,
which includes and connects both of them,
therefore the redemption was in a manner that miracle and nature were joined together,
the unification of Havayah and Elokim.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation of Ein Sof above Sovev and Memaleh unites miracle and nature, but the fact that nature itself did not conceal the miracle came from the revelation of the true root of Malchus itself.
section.t: And it can be said,
that the revelation of Ein Sof which is above Sovev and Memaleh in the union of miracle
(whose root is from Sovev)
and nature
(whose root is from Memaleh)
is only that there is felt in them a matter that is above both of them,
through which they become united.
But that nature itself was then in a manner that did not conceal or hide the miracle,
to the extent that even the opponents
[who remained then in their strength]
were nevertheless compelled to assist
[and through their strength]
in the liberation and redemption,
this is through that in Malchus itself
(the root of created beings)
its true root was revealed.
And based on this, the connection and relevance of the redemption to the psalm "Tefillah L'Moshe" will be understood even more,
the prayer of a wealthy man,
the matter of the prayer of a wealthy man is regarding a certain province etc., decree that it be built,
the drawing down of the revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof into Malchus.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through the union of miracle and nature in the redemption, power was given to draw faith into intellect and to disseminate the wellsprings of inner Torah outwardly, preparing for the ultimate revelation that all flesh will see Godliness.
section.t: And to add,
that through the union of miracle and nature that was in the redemption,
power was given to all who walk in the ways of the master of the redemption,
that faith which is above intellect
(miracle)
should be drawn down also into intellect
(nature),
and that intellect should not conceal or hide the faith.
And likewise, regarding the matter of "your wellsprings will spread forth outward"
[which began with the redemption of Yud-Tes Kislev,
and was further added to in the redemption of Yud-Beis Tammuz]
that through the union of miracle and nature that was in the redemption, power was given to disseminate the wellsprings of the inner dimension of the Torah
(which is above the world,
miracle)
outward,
and in a manner that even when they are found outwardly, it is openly seen that they are the wellsprings of the inner dimension of the Torah.
And that even when they are found outwardly, they are in a manner that one sees openly that they are wellsprings,
this is not only because the wellsprings are in revelation, but also because the "outward" is made in a way that does not conceal or hide the wellsprings,
and furthermore,
it becomes a vessel for the wellsprings.
And this is a close preparation for the fulfillment of the prophecy "And the glory of Havayah will be revealed, and all flesh together will see that the mouth of Havayah has spoken,"
that the flesh will see Godliness
(not only from the aspect of the revelation of the glory of Havayah,
but also)
from the aspect of the flesh itself.
